choices.content: It is independent of the included angle.
It is negative, and the square of the third side's length is less than the sum of the squares of the other two sides' lengths.

question.prompt: In the law of cosines, what can be said about the term \(−2ab\cos C\) when the included angle is acute?

solutions.explanation: The cosine of an acute angle is positive. Subtracting a positive number makes the result smaller than the sum of the squares of the two sides.
solutions.title: Sign of the cosine correction
